```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.5)
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

* Citation: Gulati A, Isbister GK, Duffull SB. Scale reduction of a systems
  coagulation model with an application to modeling
  pharmacokinetic-pharmacodynamic data. *CPT Pharmacometrics Syst Pharmacol*.
  2014;3(1):e90.
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1038/psp.2013.67> (open access,
  [PMC3910010](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3910010/))
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Gulati_2014_brownSnakeVenom"))$description`

Gulati 2014 reduced the 62-state, 178-parameter humoral coagulation network of
Wajima 2009 (as extended for Australian elapid venoms) to five states by proper
lumping, keeping only what the brown snake venom to fibrinogen input-output
relationship needs. The ODEs of the lumped system were then written out by
hand (the "extracted model", Eq 1-5), two unidentifiable parameters were held
at their original-model values, and the remaining nine were estimated as a
population PK-PD model on fibrinogen concentrations from the Australian
Snakebite Project. This file packages that fitted extracted model.

# Population

The data came from the Australian Snakebite Project, which recruited 138
snakebite cases from over 100 Australian hospitals between January 2004 and
May 2008 (Methods, "The data"). Of 73 patients bitten by brown snakes, the 61
with complete venom-induced consumption coagulopathy (VICC) contributed timed
fibrinogen concentrations (Table 3). Patients were 74% male with a mean age of
41 years (SD 18). Every complete-VICC patient received antivenom. Fibrinogen
was measured in g/L with a limit of quantification of 0.2 g/L, and data below
it were handled with Beal's M3 method in NONMEM 7.2 (FOCE with interaction).
Because the venom dose is unknown, every patient was given the same nominal
venom dose and the between-subject variability on its bioavailable fraction
absorbs the bite-to-bite differences.

# Source trace

| Model element | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Venom absorption state `depot`, `d/dt(depot) = -ka * depot` | dose 0.0075 (nmol/L) | Eq 1; Table 1 state 1L |
| Venom plasma state `central`, elimination times antivenom factor | factor 1 or 100 | Eq 2 |
| Fibrinogen `fibrinogen`, production, loss, thrombin-driven conversion | `fibrinogen(0)` 8945.5 nmol/L | Eq 3 |
| Thrombin `thrombin`, venom-driven formation, first-order loss | `thrombin(0)` 0 | Eq 4 |
| Lumped pool `lumped`, production, loss, venom-driven activation | `lumped(0)` 1394.4 nmol/L | Eq 5; Table 1 state 5L |
| `ka` (k_a^Brown) | 0.854 1/h | Table 2 |
| `kel` (d^Brown) | 0.744 1/h | Table 2 |
| `kdeg_thrombin` (d^IIa) | 58.3 1/h | Table 2 |
| `vmax_lumped` (vmax, lumped state to IIa by venom) | 1940 | Table 2 |
| `km_lumped` (Km, lumped state to IIa by venom) | 1.38 nmol/L | Table 2 |
| `kdeg_fibrinogen` (d^Fg) | 0.0174 1/h | Table 2 |
| `kin_fibrinogen` (p^Fg) | 216 nmol/L/h | Table 2 |
| `vmax_fibrinogen` (vmax, Fg to F by IIa) | 8.88 | Table 2 |
| `km_fibrinogen` (Km, Fg to F by IIa) | 22.9 nmol/L | Table 2 |
| `kin_lumped` (p^Lumped_state), held constant | 147 nmol/L/h | Results, "Identifiability of the simplified model" |
| `kdeg_lumped` (d^Lumped_state), held constant | 0.01 1/h | Results, "Identifiability of the simplified model" |
| `fdepot` typical value, held constant | 1 | Methods, "Data analysis using a population approach" |

# Typical-value time course

The lumping simulations in the paper used one nominal brown snake bite
(0.0075 nmol/L) with antivenom 4 h after the bite, the average time in the
brown snake data. The chunk below solves the typical patient under that
scenario and, for contrast, without antivenom.

```{r events}
mod <- readModelDb("Gulati_2014_brownSnakeVenom")
VENOM_DOSE <- 0.0075 # Eq 1, C1L(0)
LOQ <- 0.2 # g/L, Methods "The data"

# One bite at time 0; CONMED_ANTIVENOM switches to 1 at the antivenom time
# (Inf = never given). Observations are on the fibrinogen state; rxode2
# returns Cfibrinogen and every other state at those rows.
make_events <- function(id, t_av, obs_times) {
  obs_times <- sort(unique(c(obs_times, if (is.finite(t_av)) t_av)))
  dplyr::bind_rows(
    data.frame(id = id, time = 0, amt = VENOM_DOSE, evid = 1L, cmt = "depot"),
    data.frame(id = id, time = obs_times, amt = 0, evid = 0L, cmt = "fibrinogen")
  ) |>
    dplyr::mutate(CONMED_ANTIVENOM = as.integer(time >= t_av)) |>
    dplyr::arrange(id, time, dplyr::desc(evid))
}

obs_fine <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, 2, by = 0.05), seq(2, 72, by = 0.5))))
ev_typ <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  make_events(1, 4, obs_fine) |> dplyr::mutate(arm = "Antivenom at 4 h"),
  make_events(2, Inf, obs_fine) |> dplyr::mutate(arm = "No antivenom")
)

mod_typ <- rxode2::zeroRe(mod)
sim_typ <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_typ, ev_typ, keep = "arm", returnType = "data.frame")
```

```{r typical-plot, fig.height = 6}
sim_typ |>
  dplyr::select(time, arm, `Venom plasma (nmol/L)` = central,
                `Thrombin (nmol/L)` = thrombin, `Lumped pool (nmol/L)` = lumped,
                `Fibrinogen (g/L)` = Cfibrinogen) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(-c(time, arm)) |>
  ggplot(aes(time, value, colour = arm)) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~name, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(x = "Time post-bite (h)", y = NULL, colour = NULL,
       title = "Typical brown snake envenoming, with and without antivenom") +
  theme_bw() + theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

Fibrinogen falls from 3.0 g/L to below the 0.2 g/L limit of quantification
within an hour of the bite, as the venom converts the lumped prothrombin-like
pool to thrombin, and recovers at close to the zero-order production rate once
the venom has gone. Compare the shape with Figure 2c (lumped 5-state model with
the original-model parameters), which reaches about 2.2 g/L at 40 h; the fitted
model below reaches about 2 g/L.

```{r typical-table}
sim_typ |>
  dplyr::filter(time %in% c(0, 1, 4, 10, 20, 30, 40)) |>
  dplyr::select(arm, time, Cfibrinogen) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = arm, values_from = Cfibrinogen) |>
  dplyr::rename(`Time (h)` = time) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "Typical fibrinogen (g/L).")
```

# Closed-form checks

Three quantities follow from Table 2 alone. The paper reports a brown snake
venom half-life of 55 min and a fibrinogen half-life of 1.5 days.

```{r closed-form}
p <- rxode2::rxode(mod)$theta
kel <- exp(p[["lkel"]])
kdeg_fg <- exp(p[["lkdeg_fibrinogen"]])
kin_fg <- exp(p[["lkin_fibrinogen"]])
mw <- p[["mw_fibrinogen"]]

closed <- tibble::tibble(
  Quantity = c("Venom half-life without antivenom (min)",
               "Fibrinogen half-life (days)",
               "Fibrinogen steady state kin/kdeg (g/L)",
               "Fibrinogen initial condition (g/L)"),
  Model = c(60 * log(2) / kel, log(2) / kdeg_fg / 24,
            kin_fg / kdeg_fg * mw / 1e6, p[["bl_fibrinogen"]] * mw / 1e6),
  Paper = c(55, 1.5, NA, NA)
)
knitr::kable(closed, digits = 2)

stopifnot(abs(closed$Model[1] - 55) < 2)
```

The venom half-life reproduces the reported 55 min. The fibrinogen half-life
from Table 2 is 1.66 days, which the Discussion rounds to "1.5 days".

The fibrinogen initial condition (8945.5 nmol/L, Eq 3) is not the steady state
of Eq 3 (kin / kdeg = 12414 nmol/L, 4.2 g/L), so an unbitten typical patient
drifts upward with the fibrinogen half-life. The solve below checks the
packaged ODE against the closed-form solution of that drift; both sides use the
same parameters, so the bound is tight.

```{r no-venom-drift}
ev_none <- make_events(1, Inf, c(0, 24, 48, 96, 200)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(amt = ifelse(evid == 1L, 0, amt))
drift <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_typ, ev_none, returnType = "data.frame") |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    closed = (kin_fg / kdeg_fg + (p[["bl_fibrinogen"]] - kin_fg / kdeg_fg) *
      exp(-kdeg_fg * time)) * mw / 1e6,
    pct_diff = 100 * (Cfibrinogen - closed) / closed
  )
knitr::kable(dplyr::select(drift, `Time (h)` = time, `ODE (g/L)` = Cfibrinogen,
                           `Closed form (g/L)` = closed),
             digits = 3, caption = "Fibrinogen without a bite.")
stopifnot(max(abs(drift$pct_diff)) < 0.1)
```

# Visual predictive check (Figure 3)

Figure 3 of Gulati 2014 is a percentile VPC of the final model over the
observed design (1,000 replicates, below-limit values censored as in the
data). The individual antivenom times of the observed design are not
published, so the replicate below gives every simulated patient antivenom at
4 h, the average reported for the brown snake data, and adds a sensitivity
scenario at 8 h. Values below the 0.2 g/L limit are displayed at 0.1 g/L, so
percentiles in the censored region read 0.1. The reference points are the
model-prediction percentiles read off Figure 3 by the maintainers at 20, 30 and
40 h.

```{r vpc-sim}
N_PER_ARM <- 200
obs_vpc <- c(0, 0.5, 1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 8, 10, 12, 15, 20, 25, 30, 35, 40)
ev_vpc <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  lapply(seq_len(N_PER_ARM), function(i) make_events(i, 4, obs_vpc)) |>
    dplyr::bind_rows() |> dplyr::mutate(arm = "Antivenom at 4 h"),
  lapply(seq_len(N_PER_ARM), function(i) make_events(N_PER_ARM + i, 8, obs_vpc)) |>
    dplyr::bind_rows() |> dplyr::mutate(arm = "Antivenom at 8 h")
)

rxode2::rxSetSeed(20140101)
sim_vpc <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, ev_vpc, keep = "arm", returnType = "data.frame") |>
  dplyr::filter(time %in% obs_vpc) |>
  dplyr::mutate(dv = ifelse(sim < LOQ, LOQ / 2, sim))

vpc <- sim_vpc |>
  dplyr::group_by(arm, time) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    p10 = quantile(dv, 0.1), p50 = quantile(dv, 0.5), p90 = quantile(dv, 0.9),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

fig3 <- tibble::tibble(
  time = c(20, 30, 40),
  p10 = c(0.45, 0.65, 0.95),
  p50 = c(0.75, 1.25, 1.75),
  p90 = c(1.30, 2.20, 3.15)
)
```

```{r vpc-plot}
vpc |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(c(p10, p50, p90), names_to = "pct") |>
  ggplot(aes(time, value, colour = arm, linetype = pct == "p50", group = interaction(arm, pct))) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point(
    data = tidyr::pivot_longer(fig3, c(p10, p50, p90), names_to = "pct"),
    aes(time, value), inherit.aes = FALSE, shape = 4, size = 3
  ) +
  scale_linetype_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = "solid", `FALSE` = "dashed"), guide = "none") +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 6)) +
  labs(x = "Time post-bite (h)", y = "Fibrinogen (g/L)", colour = NULL,
       title = "10th, 50th and 90th percentiles of simulated fibrinogen",
       caption = "Replicates Figure 3 of Gulati 2014; crosses are the Figure 3 model-prediction percentiles.") +
  theme_bw() + theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

```{r vpc-table}
vpc_cmp <- vpc |>
  dplyr::filter(time %in% fig3$time) |>
  dplyr::left_join(fig3, by = "time", suffix = c("", "_fig3"))
knitr::kable(
  dplyr::select(vpc_cmp, Scenario = arm, `Time (h)` = time,
                `P10 sim` = p10, `P10 Fig 3` = p10_fig3,
                `P50 sim` = p50, `P50 Fig 3` = p50_fig3,
                `P90 sim` = p90, `P90 Fig 3` = p90_fig3),
  digits = 2, caption = "Simulated versus Figure 3 percentiles (g/L)."
)

at40 <- dplyr::filter(vpc_cmp, time == 40, arm == "Antivenom at 4 h")
stopifnot(
  # Centre: a wrong production rate, loss rate or unit conversion moves the
  # recovery by tens of percent.
  abs(at40$p50 / at40$p50_fig3 - 1) < 0.25,
  # Spread: the 10th percentile at 40 h separates the two readings of the
  # residual-error row (about 0.9 g/L with a 39% proportional SD, about 0.4
  # g/L with a 62% SD).
  at40$p10 > 0.6
)
```

At 40 h the simulated percentiles match Figure 3. At 20 and 30 h the simulated
median with antivenom at 4 h is 0.3 to 0.4 g/L above Figure 3, i.e. recovery
starts a few hours earlier; the 8 h scenario sits closer, consistent with the
observed design containing patients treated later than the 4 h average.

# PKNCA: venom disposition

The venom states carry the model's PK. A PKNCA pass on the typical patient's
plasma venom state recovers the venom half-life without antivenom. With
antivenom at 4 h, plasma venom is cleared 100 times faster from then on, so
its terminal phase becomes absorption-limited: the half-life PKNCA reports for
that scenario is ln(2) / ka = 0.81 h, set by the venom still leaving the bite
site, and the venom AUC is smaller.

```{r pknca}
conc_venom <- sim_typ |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(central)) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, arm, central)
dose_venom <- ev_typ |>
  dplyr::filter(evid == 1L) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, amt, arm)

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc_venom, central ~ time | arm + id)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_venom, amt ~ time | arm + id)
intervals <- data.frame(start = 0, end = 72, cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE,
                        auclast = TRUE, half.life = TRUE)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))

knitr::kable(
  as.data.frame(nca_res) |>
    dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("cmax", "tmax", "auclast", "half.life")) |>
    dplyr::select(arm, PPTESTCD, PPORRES) |>
    tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = PPORRES) |>
    dplyr::rename(Scenario = arm, `Cmax (nmol/L)` = cmax, `Tmax (h)` = tmax,
                  `AUC0-72 (nmol*h/L)` = auclast, `t1/2 (h)` = half.life),
  digits = 4, caption = "NCA of plasma venom, typical patient."
)
```

## Comparison against published values

The paper reports only the venom half-life (Discussion, 55 min without
antivenom).

```{r nca-compare}
published <- tibble::tibble(arm = "No antivenom", half.life = 55 / 60)
cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = nca_res,
  reference = published,
  by = "arm",
  params = "half.life",
  units = c(half.life = "h"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)
knitr::kable(cmp, caption = "Simulated versus published venom half-life. * differs by >20%.")
```

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Residual-error row read as an SD.** Table 2 labels the proportional
  residual-error row `sigma^2_prop = 0.390`. Read as a variance (SD 0.624), the
  simulated 10th percentile at 40 h is about 0.4 g/L, against about 0.95 g/L in
  the paper's own VPC (Figure 3), and the 90th percentile at time 0 is about
  5.6 g/L against about 4.8 g/L. Read as an SD (39% CV), both match. The
  packaged model therefore uses `propSd = 0.390`. The additive row
  (`sigma^2_add = 0.00100`) is used as a variance (SD 0.032 g/L); either
  reading is negligible next to the 0.2 g/L limit of quantification.
* **BSV rows are variances.** The Table 2 BSV rows are headed "(%)" but carry
  values (0.005 to 2.10) that cannot be percentages of CV given the reported
  shrinkage; they are used as NONMEM OMEGA variances of exponential random
  effects, as the Methods describe. The VPC above is insensitive to this
  choice because the residual error dominates the prediction interval.
* **Fibrinogen units.** The model states are in nmol/L but fibrinogen was
  measured in g/L, and the source does not print the conversion. The packaged
  observation uses a fibrinogen molecular weight of 340 kDa, which puts the
  Eq 3 initial condition at 3.04 g/L, matching the start of the curves in
  Figures 2 and 3. `mw_fibrinogen` can be changed in `ini()`.
* **Extracted versus lumped initial conditions.** Table 1 lists lumped-model
  initial conditions of 8,900 nmol/L for fibrinogen and 7,900 nmol/L for the
  lumped state (the sum of the 58 pooled original states), which the
  lumping simulations used. The fitted extracted model writes its own initial
  conditions in Eq 3 and Eq 5 (8945.5 and 1394.4 nmol/L, the latter being the
  original model's prothrombin, which the lumped state is assumed to be
  dominated by). The packaged model uses the Eq 3 and Eq 5 values.
* **Not at steady state.** With the Table 2 and held-constant values, neither
  fibrinogen (kin / kdeg = 12414 nmol/L) nor the lumped pool (147 / 0.01 =
  14700 nmol/L) starts at the steady state of its own equation. This is a
  property of the published model and is reproduced as is.
* **Antivenom timing.** Eq 2 switches venom elimination 100-fold when
  antivenom is present. The model takes this from the time-varying covariate
  `CONMED_ANTIVENOM`. The paper does not say whether the NONMEM fit used each
  patient's antivenom time or the 4 h average; supply each patient's own time
  when it is known.
* **Venom dose.** Eq 1 sets the venom absorption state to 0.0075 (nmol/L) at
  the bite; the Methods also call the same nominal dose "0.0075 mg". The model
  takes it as a dose of 0.0075 into `depot`, scaled by the bioavailable
  fraction (typical value 1, between-subject variance 1.40).
* **Vmax units.** Table 2 prints both Vmax values in nmol/L/h, but in Eq 3-5
  each multiplies a concentration, so they act as first-order rate constants
  (1/h). The paper notes that these Vmax and Km values do not carry their
  usual enzyme-kinetic meaning.
* **Below-limit data.** The M3 likelihood for data below 0.2 g/L is part of
  the estimation, not the model; simulated values below the limit are only
  censored for display here.
